title: Indra OCR: 18 MB Local OCR, 49 Pages a Second on CPU
status: Owner approved Indra OCR on 2026-10-15 for one artifact-only video. No public Release, no Buffer scheduling or posting. Approved Option-3 Chatterbox flow voice; no on-screen credit captions.

facts.authors_cpu_test: 49.4 pages/s on 32 x86 CPU cores, OCR mode, 300 OmniParseBench pages
facts.checked: 2026-10-15, GitHub REST API + Hugging Face model API

credits_on_screen: Own synthetic invoice, own local OCR output and own proof-card visual. Source links in post/description only. No on-screen credits.
verify_before_render: GitHub API checked 2026-10-15 08:01 UTC: 282 stars, 24 forks; repository created 2026-10-13; code license Apache-2.0. Radar's 282 stars/day uses whole-day age; corrected rate at check time was about 150 stars/day and is not spoken.
README: local CLI/viewer; PDFs and images to Markdown, plain text or JSON with boxes and reading order; about 18 MB of models; no PyTorch.

Speed is the project authors' benchmark, not ours: OCR mode 7.3 pages/s on 4 cores and 49.4 pages/s on 32 cores on the same x86 no-GPU machine and 300 OmniParseBench pages. Say 'the authors measured' and name the core count.

Our own test: indra-ocr 0.3.2, --mode ocr on a self-generated image-only synthetic invoice (no real customer data) recovered both item rows and the PKR 1,360 total. One sandbox timing is not spoken as a benchmark.

License split is mandatory: code Apache-2.0; model weights use a modified OpenRAIL-M license with restrictions, including no use competing with Datalab's API. Never call the whole project unrestricted Apache-2.0.

Limitations are mandatory: built for clean print; handwriting unsupported; degraded/old scans score poorly; scanned-image OCR does not cover Arabic/Urdu (digital PDFs with an existing text layer are different).
Use only the synthetic test assets in captures/repo-indra-01; no personal documents, third-party creator clips, or copied demo media. No on-screen credit captions.

scenes.heading: BEFORE YOU *TRUST IT*
scenes.say: The catches: handwriting is unsupported, faded scans score poorly, and the weights carry restricted {OpenRAIL-M|Open Rail M} terms. The code is Apache two, and our clean print test recovered the total.
Would you use local OCR? Comment INDRA and I will pin the repo.

youtube.title: Indra OCR: 18 MB Local OCR, 49 Pages a Second on CPU
youtube.description:
Indra OCR turns PDFs and images into Markdown, plain text or JSON with boxes and reading order, locally on CPU. In the project authors' benchmark it reached 49.4 pages/s on 32 CPU cores (OCR mode); our own OCR-only test on a synthetic invoice recovered both item rows and the total. The catches: it is built for clean print, handwriting is unsupported, faded scans score poorly, and while the code is Apache-2.0 the model weights use a restricted modified OpenRAIL-M license.
Source: https://github.com/datalab-to/indra
